knowledge:
- key_parameters: ontology=Specifies the GO category of interest ("BP", "MF", or "CC") ;; allGenes=A named numeric or factor vector where names are gene identifiers and values are scores or binary indicators ;; geneSel=A function that accepts gene scores and returns a logical vector indicating which genes are significant (required if allGenes is numeric) ;; nodeSize=An integer (default 1, recommended 5-10) used to prune the GO hierarchy of terms with fewer than nodeSize annotated genes ;; annot=An annotation function mapping gene IDs to GO terms (e.g., annFUN.db, annFUN.org, annFUN.gene2GO, annFUN.file) ;; algorithm=The topology-aware method to use ("classic", "elim", "weight", "weight01", "lea", "parentchild") ;; statistic=The statistical test to apply ("fisher", "ks", "t", "globaltest", "sum", "ks.ties")
- alternatives: genefilter is recommended for preprocessing and filtering low-variance/low-expression genes before running topGO ;; multtest (via getPvalues) is used for calculating differential expression p-values.
- when_to_use: Use when performing functional enrichment analysis on gene expression data (microarray, RNA-seq) or predefined gene lists, especially when you want to reduce redundancy and false positives caused by the hierarchical dependencies of GO terms.
- pitfalls: Not all statistical tests are compatible with all topology algorithms (e.g., the weight algorithm does not work with score-based tests like Kolmogorov-Smirnov) ;; Standard multiple testing corrections (FDR/FWER) are highly conservative and theoretically problematic for topology-aware methods (like elim and weight) because the tests are dependent ;; Aggressive gene filtering is necessary to avoid overly conservative adjusted p-values, but filtering too strictly can discard truly significant genes.

workflows.name: predefined_gene_list_enrichment
workflows.intent: Perform GO enrichment analysis using a predefined list of interesting genes and custom gene-to-GO annotations.
input: geneid2go.map (tab-separated text file mapping gene IDs to comma-separated GO terms)
myInterestingGenes (character vector of predefined interesting genes)
workflows.stages:
1. Read custom gene-to-GO mappings from a file.
2. Define the gene universe and create a named factor vector indicating interesting genes.
3. Initialize the topGOdata object using the custom mapping.
4. Run a count-based enrichment test (Fisher's exact test).
5. Generate a summary table of the top significant GO terms.
workflows.code:
geneID2GO <- readMappings(file = system.file("examples/geneid2go.map", package = "topGO"))
GO2geneID <- inverseList(geneID2GO)
geneNames <- names(geneID2GO)
myInterestingGenes <- sample(geneNames, length(geneNames) / 10)
geneList <- factor(as.integer(geneNames %in% myInterestingGenes))
names(geneList) <- geneNames
GOdata <- new("topGOdata", ontology = "MF", allGenes = geneList, annot = annFUN.gene2GO, gene2GO = geneID2GO)
resultFis <- runTest(GOdata, algorithm = "classic", statistic = "fisher")
allRes <- GenTable(GOdata, classic = resultFis, orderBy = "classic", topNodes = 20)

workflows.name: score_based_expression_enrichment
workflows.intent: Perform GO enrichment analysis using continuous gene-wise scores (such as differential expression p-values) and a chip annotation database.
input: ALL (ExpressionSet containing normalized microarray expression measurements)
y (integer vector of binary class labels for samples)
workflows.stages:
1. Filter low-expression and low-variance probes.
2. Compute gene-wise p-values for differential expression.
3. Define a selection function to identify significant genes based on p-values.
4. Initialize the topGOdata object using a Bioconductor chip annotation package.
5. Run multiple enrichment tests (classic Fisher, classic KS, and elim KS).
6. Generate a comparative summary table of the results.
7. Visualize gene score distributions and the significant GO subgraphs.
workflows.code:
library(topGO)
library(ALL)
data(ALL)
library(genefilter)
selProbes <- genefilter(ALL, filterfun(pOverA(0.20, log2(100)), function(x) (IQR(x) > 0.25)))
eset <- ALL[selProbes, ]
y <- as.integer(sapply(eset$BT, function(x) return(substr(x, 1, 1) == 'T')))
geneList <- getPvalues(exprs(eset), classlabel = y, alternative = "greater")
topDiffGenes <- function(allScore) {
  return(allScore < 0.01)
}
affyLib <- paste(annotation(ALL), "db", sep = ".")
library(package = affyLib, character.only = TRUE)
GOdata <- new("topGOdata", 
              description = "GO analysis of ALL data; B-cell vs T-cell",
              ontology = "BP",
              allGenes = geneList,
              geneSel = topDiffGenes,
              annot = annFUN.db,
              nodeSize = 5,
              affyLib = affyLib)
resultFis <- runTest(GOdata, algorithm = "classic", statistic = "fisher")
resultKS <- runTest(GOdata, algorithm = "classic", statistic = "ks")
resultKS.elim <- runTest(GOdata, algorithm = "elim", statistic = "ks")
allRes <- GenTable(GOdata, classic = resultFis, KS = resultKS, elim = resultKS.elim, orderBy = "elim", topNodes = 20)
goID <- allRes[1, "GO.ID"]
print(showGroupDensity(GOdata, goID, ranks = TRUE))
gt <- printGenes(GOdata, whichTerms = goID, chip = affyLib, numChar = 40)
showSigOfNodes(GOdata, score(resultKS.elim), firstSigNodes = 5, useInfo = 'all')
